| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31976620-c820-4ff7-b614-dc9a690c9b64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In March, [QatarEnergy declared ](https://substack.com/redirect/597f4696-1cc7-4d3c-805b-7a951f4f3649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[force majeure](https://substack.com/redirect/597f4696-1cc7-4d3c-805b-7a951f4f3649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ on its natural gas exports. One announcement, one simple sentence. And just like that, twenty percent of the world's liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply went offline. Seven months later, it's still dark. [In the first six months of the war](https://substack.com/redirect/c259ed63-5af1-4a9f-90e3-a9e779c96c44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Qatar shipped 18 LNG cargoes. In the same period the year before, it shipped 509. The lost sales are valued at around $24 billion. As of this writing, there's still no firm date for resumption.
Natural gas supplies [about a quarter of the world's energy](https://substack.com/redirect/85ac9fe1-ae58-48ed-8b50-f79a945861a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and LNG (gas chilled to negative 162 degrees Celsius until it liquefies and shrinks to one six-hundredth of its volume) is how it crosses oceans to countries that need it most. If you're unfamiliar with how this actually happens, you'll find the two minute video below worthwhile.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d7f22229-948e-4bfd-adc6-93b7c505ce4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The importance of LNG is hard to overstate. It generates 28% of Pakistan's electricity and half of Bangladesh's; it heats homes across Europe and Asia; and Qatar, shipping one of every five cargoes on earth, was the market's anchor. But LNG isn't just fuel. It's also feedstock for the fertilizer that grows the world's food, for plastics such as IV bags and syringes, and for roughly a third of the world's helium (which is used to cool MRI machines and data centers). When the LNG market is disrupted, the ripples don't stop at your electricity bill. They reach your grocery store, your hospital, and even your hosted cloud services.
Many people think of energy production the way they think of a light switch. A simple decision can flip it off or flip it on. LNG doesn't work that way. An LNG plant is a cryogenic facility operating at temperatures that can freeze steel and make it brittle. Shutting one down is a [deliberate, staged process](https://substack.com/redirect/f06b4d78-457e-4184-a9f4-e84e71364404?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that must be carefully managed. It begins by reducing production to a minimum, stopping the flow of gas, and easing the pressure on upstream facilities to protect equipment.
But surely storage can mitigate the impact of a shutdown, right? Wrong. Qatar's storage tanks at [Ras Laffan (the hub of Qatar's LNG industry)](https://substack.com/redirect/82c88d87-385f-44ca-a2a3-be58767f468c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fill up in less than two days when the effort runs at normal production rates. Once full, there is no choice but to shut down.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c60734ba-9cbf-44a3-9be3-56c73a1ec8a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Restarting is even more difficult than the shutdown. The process to turn on the system is deliberately slow to avoid thermal shock. Cool too quickly and you'll crack the equipment. Multiple liquefaction trains also can't restart at the same time; they have to be sequenced, one by one. QatarEnergy estimates it will take [at least two weeks](https://substack.com/redirect/597f4696-1cc7-4d3c-805b-7a951f4f3649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to restart, then another two weeks to reach full capacity. That's a full month in the **best** case scenario--assuming no damage, no complications, and a secure shipping lane. But there is damage that must be repaired, complications that have to be addressed, and a shipping lane that remains insecure. It's more likely, therefore, that _**the process to restart the system could take years**_.
Iranian missiles struck Ras Laffan in March, [destroying two liquefaction trains](https://substack.com/redirect/1199d39b-6d35-42ec-b8cc-3cbd3b6c4adc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); that's 17% of Qatar's total capacity. Analysts suggest it might take up to **three years** to repair. The remaining undamaged trains could restart in weeks once the Strait of Hormuz is secure, but the strait is far from secure. The [IEA estimates](https://substack.com/redirect/c235d13b-857f-4e82-b15e-39c8cf11b486?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the conflict will strip 120 billion cubic meters from global LNG supply between 2026 and 2030. Analysts say a comfortable supply-demand balance won't return until 2028.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6c68a94f-4707-43e9-b10f-805a720c933a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The news is not all bad, however. Qatar's [North Field East expansion](https://substack.com/redirect/b2b9faf4-5719-4844-9bea-df5882d453e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (a massive project begun before the war) is planning to have its first train ready to run in November. It's expected to be producing by the first quarter of 2027. More trains will follow through 2027 and 2028, with Qatar's capacity expected to double from 77 million tons per year to 142 million. Of course, these numbers assume no disruption to the North Field East project.
Meanwhile, the energy dominoes have begun falling around the world. [EU gas storage](https://substack.com/redirect/c235d13b-857f-4e82-b15e-39c8cf11b486?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sits 30% below its five-year average. European and Asian buyers are competing for the same LNG cargoes, bidding against each other in a market that was tight before Hormuz was closed. LNG freight rates and spot prices have hit multi-year highs.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1661999&post_id=220841653&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIwODQxNjUzLCJpYXQiOjE3OTIzMzM5MzgsImV4cCI6MTc5NDkyNTkzOCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE2NjE5OTkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.QlmXoUIAkF32QfY_HIb44kEgoB5YKqh4GwFz-wAe6M0)
The consequences of the LNG disruption are far from abstract, especially if you live in a colder part of the world. New England, for instance, generates [more than half its electricity from natural gas](https://substack.com/redirect/b1a2886e-8fba-48f3-b4cf-48706fed66d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and during arctic blasts, LNG can supply [up to 35% of the region's total gas](https://substack.com/redirect/4ab38fc2-a503-4701-a639-ce7081a500f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Pipeline capacity from Appalachia is constrained and storage is negligible. When cold snaps have hit in January, wholesale electricity prices have previously [spiked to $441 per megawatt-hour](https://substack.com/redirect/4ab38fc2-a503-4701-a639-ce7081a500f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's triple the monthly average, and worse, that was **before** twenty percent of the world's LNG went offline. And because the energy markets are interconnected, what happens in the Northeast will not stay in the Northeast. Expect a wave of higher costs to spread across the country.
And that bill will land on a consumer who was already stretched thin and worried about his or her budget. The [University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index](https://substack.com/redirect/5e851e0f-f9cc-4d9e-bddf-c0de2c71f024?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fell to 46.3 in October, a five-month low and within sight of its all-time trough, with the gauge of current conditions plunging 12% in a single month. The survey director's summary was blunt: "Frustration over cost-of-living continues to mount." Little wonder. [Consumer prices rose 3.7%](https://substack.com/redirect/81288ced-8daf-4e6d-b40d-5b14574b5421?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over the past year, but energy rose 20%, and gasoline is up 34% and has sat above $4 a gallon since midsummer. Households now expect 4.7% inflation over the coming year, and they are bracing accordingly.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4291c541-7fd3-4ae6-95ae-1b318b1a85c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Now look at paychecks. The [September jobs report](https://substack.com/redirect/f63a07fb-8e12-4fb0-a39a-82a81bf0b77a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) showed the economy added just 29,000 jobs, unemployment ticked up to 4.2%, and wages grew 3.0%, the slowest pace of the post-pandemic cycle. After inflation, _**real earnings fell for the sixth consecutive month**_. Bottom line: each paycheck buys less than it did a year ago.
To cope with the situation, Americans have been bridging the gap with borrowed money. [Credit card balances hit a record $1.26 trillion](https://substack.com/redirect/56672e66-3e26-448c-be52-76d736f1b2a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the second quarter, and the share of card debt newly falling 90 or more days behind is running near 7% annualized, a level the New York Fed itself calls "elevated." Auto loans are deteriorating at a similar pace. The mortgage picture is worse where it matters most: the [share of seriously delinquent mortgages has risen for four consecutive quarters](https://substack.com/redirect/11ebeee3-71ef-48ba-ba13-c265ad8c1932?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and FHA loans (used disproportionately by first-time buyers and entry-level borrowers) are now nearly 12% delinquent, up more than a full percentage point in a year. The inventory of homes in foreclosure is up by around 20% over the same period. The household balance sheet, in other words, has no slack left in it.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6344ca71-7988-40b8-80ef-13f28f219e65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In the midst of this pain, winter is coming. The Energy Information Administration's [Winter Fuels Outlook](https://substack.com/redirect/323b8d52-8fa7-4a3b-81ed-391c543b95e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), published October 6, already forecasts the average heating-oil household paying $2,115 this winter, up 21%, as crude and tight distillate markets bite. The outlook has a more benign view of the natural gas market, driven by a belief this winter will not be as cold as normal and that US markets are self-sufficient and therefore insulated from global dynamics.
I can't judge if this winter is going to be colder or warmer than historical averages, but I do know the Northeast is not protected from global LNG dynamics. On very cold days, New England imports LNG at world prices, and world prices are being set by the same European and Asian buyers bidding for cargoes Qatar can no longer deliver. The connection is simple: cold weather raises prices, and larger increases are possible when fuel inventories are low.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c3a67f09-bc18-4aab-9469-cc360cc7e631?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I live in New Hampshire. When temperatures drops, heat is not optional. The question is what it will cost, and what gives way when a household that was already choosing between the credit card minimum and the car payment gets a bill it never budgeted for. For millions of American families, the _force majeure_ declared months ago, in a place most of them couldn't find on a map, may turn out to be the straw that breaks the camel's back. And once the camel is down, there is no switch to flip it back up.

And just like that, twenty percent of the world's liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply went offline. Seven months later, it's still dark. , Qatar shipped 18 LNG cargoes. In the same period the year before, it shipped 509. The lost sales are valued at around $24 billion. As of this writing, there's still no firm date for resumption. Natural gas supplies , and LNG (gas chilled to negative 162 degrees Celsius until it liquefies and shrinks to one six-hundredth of its volume) is how it crosses oceans to countries that need it most. It generates 28% of Pakistan's electricity and half of Bangladesh's; it heats homes across Europe and Asia; and Qatar, shipping one of every five cargoes on earth, was the market's anchor. But LNG isn't just fuel. It's also feedstock for the fertilizer that grows the world's food, for plastics such as IV bags and syringes, and for roughly a third of the world's helium (which is used to cool MRI machines and data centers). An LNG plant is a cryogenic facility operating at temperatures that can freeze steel and make it brittle. Shutting one down is a that must be carefully managed. It begins by reducing production to a minimum, stopping the flow of gas, and easing the pressure on upstream facilities to protect equipment. But surely storage can mitigate the impact of a shutdown, right? Wrong. Qatar's storage tanks at fill up in less than two days when the effort runs at normal production rates. | Peter,
Louisiana is MAGA's death star. It is the place where they test their most policies before firing them off at the rest of the country.
This summer alone, they canceled an ongoing election under a fake "state of emergency" and eliminated one of our majority-Black Democratic districts.
They passed a bill forcing homeless people into indentured servitude. They criminalized abortion. They deployed the National Guard into our streets. They tortured immigrants at the Winn Correctional Center in North Louisiana.
But a rebellion is brewing in the Bayou.
A catastrophic vulnerability has been found in MAGA's death star, and we are about to blow it wide open. Trump's approval rating in the state is underwater. Voters are fed up with the foreign wars, an economy on the brink of collapse, and National Guard and ICE storm troopers patrolling our own streets.

Losing Louisiana would be a catastrophic defeat for MAGA in the very state they built as their death star. And winning this Senate seat could all but guarantee Democrats flip the chamber. That is a move that could save the republic.
We need every Democrat to rally to this cause. We might not get another shot at an upset like this. | | Dear Fellow American, It's hard growing up. But can you imagine growing up never knowing your father? Telemachus did. His father, Odysseus, left for the Trojan War shortly after he was born. Twenty years later, he still hadn't returned. Without a father to guide him, Telemachus had to learn courage, judgment, and responsibility on his own--all while men seeking to replace his father took over his home and ate away at his family's future. In many ways, _The Odyssey_ begins not with Odysseus, but with his son. Before Odysseus returned home, Telemachus had to learn what it means to become a man. **Many young people today face a similar challenge. They are searching for direction, purpose, and examples worth following.** That is one reason _The Odyssey_ remains as relevant today as it was three thousand years ago. It speaks to the timeless task of forming good men and women capable of governing themselves and contributing to a free society. **That is why Hillsdale College launched a new FREE online course on _The Odyssey_ , along with a special educational initiative to share its timeless lessons with Americans nationwide.** **Our goal is to place this story before at least 100,000 students, parents, teachers, and lifelong learners** and encourage them to think seriously about the virtues that sustain families, communities, and free societies. **But we cannot do that without you. Will you help?** Your gift today will help more Americans encounter these permanent truths through Hillsdale's educational outreach. Whether you choose to give **$50, $100, $250,** or another amount, your support will help introduce students, parents, and lifelong learners to timeless lessons on character, responsibility, leadership, and self-government through this course and Hillsdale's other educational efforts. **Please make your gift today using this secure link:** [https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/the-odyssey-support](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/LlBbEM_TotogxQscrkxqE171-WUvfA17fLKhY9JjJk6bBrTMtVB2007lMqkt2_d5S8RiqFwSDY8xpGP2qDDfOQLI5sSXscqfZ55DOIodD9JsaYTZ4Y_RIewC1okTH7RdvPSC_lOLoCeuiXzxsDF0kHRV1BdjQlkHK27g8CbLbe1LJ8GUJfPWKNwx6qPm_pi6GLkuK_GdxEPutRHdEEgbiDS7eo_JnqMALWQX4ILmTw8jGDeHz_TsDXuedc36PkctAHk8RnS8USR_L8RdjD6bMPLs_JOBr6vgNmReFng13-Fl8-bp4-t818ozLAWbFbgJGxVtm0Mq51c-wsHdZPJ_ERHbsmJEm7rwfQauHzEJD12X-tYsph4JRSTLij3kD4Kkz5mdPcwLFOvXWyHK-WcNTuKgAQcsSIXbfJCi8aXhPl_w6xcD7-DGy97T2jaVmNqcCAb4HR9bq3XHHeV0Env31M8UjOUJh1Dmlg6qjB4vTjW0Lw4f3bTJJ-PVV-cYoG81xprurJ_4Or-V3FBfxPSDWtYm7HeUZB5_gfJwy2OaHaUF2iwZNWhd9z1sXhuNpO1oWhy32D249Av6DMWezHeYzVgklV3wnXLmD8fdro0i9NVij2eDPxA7cKUBb5FOCsT6RjvBtGYrxgtsGim9lCnKFmzWKIwvOn7Bf-icADZu3rHzgZ1EaMgkb6eRfxEYM0bChxlA5FszkZaxzm9_OKX_MS4tSLTl25uMkc7mST65tm6eEQpN/am0sqUi_7dYbnPozseN9VgMSDfULjIwh/25) Hillsdale does all this work while refusing every penny of government funding--not even indirect funding through student grants and loans. That is why Hillsdale College launched a new FREE online course on The Odyssey , along with a special educational initiative to share its timeless lessons with Americans nationwide. Our goal is to place this story before at least 100,000 students, parents, teachers, and lifelong learners and encourage them to think seriously about the virtues that sustain families, communities, and free societies. But we cannot do that without you. Will you help? Your gift today will help more Americans encounter these permanent truths through Hillsdale's educational outreach. Whether you choose to give $50, $100, $250, or another amount, your support will help introduce students, parents, and lifelong learners to timeless lessons on character, responsibility, leadership, and self-government through this course and Hillsdale's other educational efforts. Please make your gift today using this secure link: Hillsdale does all this work while refusing every penny of government funding--not even indirect funding through student grants and loans. That means this effort depends entirely on friends like you. By supporting this initiative, you can help place one of the greatest educational works ever written before thousands of students and lifelong learners as they wrestle with timeless questions about character, responsibility, leadership, and freedom. Kristalina Georgieva spent Monday handing the world's finance ministers a weather report. Artificial intelligence, the IMF's managing director told the Fund-Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok -- Reuters was in the room -- is hitting the labor market like a "slow-moving tsunami": roughly 40 percent of jobs worldwide will eventually be "augmented, downgraded or eliminated." Exposure runs to 60 percent in advanced economies and 23 percent in low-income countries -- and that is not mercy; the wave is simply "further away." And the people to worry about "first and foremost," she said, are young people -- young graduates first in line to be knocked down.
Here is the sentence that should be engraved on every pair of ribbon-cutting scissors in America: even where the overall employment balance stays positive, the IMF warns, the gains are concentrating in lower-skilled -- read, lower-paid -- work. And the rungs beneath are going first. "Normally, they would get into these routine repetitive jobs and then grow up the ranks," Georgieva said of young workers. "But if they're gone, I don't think any young person wants to be a barista in a coffee shop as [their] professional future." The Fund's staff note this year is literally titled "Bridging Skill Gaps for the Future: New Jobs Creation in the AI Age." The world's job forecasts now come with a wage forecast attached.
Hold that against the pitch you have heard at every groundbreaking since 2023. The AI buildout, we were told, would repeat the tech miracle of the 2000s -- the boom that put the internet, and a paycheck, in every county seat. This week the IMF answered, in effect: jobs are coming. They are not the ones being promised.
**The last miracle was a jobs machine**
It is worth being precise about why, because the nostalgia is doing a lot of work in the pitch. The internet was a general-purpose technology, and it went looking for labor. It put an IT department in every bank, a website behind every cash register, a warehouse in every logistics park, a help desk in every hospital. The dot-com crash was real, and it hurt -- but the job machine kept running through the decade: the Bureau of Labor Statistics projected computer-specialist employment to grow 25.2 percent from 2006 to 2016, more than twice the 10.4 percent rate for jobs overall. Labor was the input and labor was the payoff, and the gains spread, because the technology went where the people were.
The data center inverts that equation. It is the most labor-light capital project America builds: a billion-dollar box that hums. And the receipts have been accumulating for two years.
**The receipts**
Business Insider's analysis of construction permits, economic-development deals and company disclosures -- compiled by the watchdog Good Jobs First -- found that even the largest data centers generally employ fewer than 150 permanent workers, some as few as 25. Construction, the number that always headlines the press release, is short-term work, sometimes under a year -- while the tax breaks that pay for it run a decade or longer. Over the life of those abatements, the public can spend more than $2 million for every permanent, full-time job -- roughly eight times the $262,000-per-job average Good Jobs First found in ordinary economic-development megadeals in 2023. As one of the group's researchers put it: "If this were completely private money, it would be a different story. These taxpayer dollars need to actually incentivize good long-term jobs and they're not."
Virginia's own audit arm, JLARC, translated it into square footage: a typical 250,000-square-foot data center needs about 50 full-time workers. One job per 5,000 square feet of building. Sixteen of the 36 state data-center subsidy programs in the country require no job creation at all; most of the rest ask for 50 or fewer positions. New Jersey, the spendthrift, demands 100.
Food & Water Watch, mining the records of Virginia -- the industry's national flagship -- estimated that perhaps 23,000 people held permanent data-center jobs in the entire United States as of 2024. One-hundredth of one percent of American employment, in an industry absorbing an outsized share of the nation's new electricity. In Illinois, the Illinois Economic Policy Institute tallied the announced $57 billion in data-center investment: more than 120,000 jobs, yes -- mostly temporary -- and about 2,800 permanent ones. Twenty point two million dollars per permanent job.
Credit where due, because the honest version of this argument needs it: the construction phase pays. Electricians, pipefitters and ironworkers have been the one place this boom genuinely shows up in paychecks, and the work is skilled. But a construction peak is a crest, not a ladder. It ends, and it belongs to whoever owns the next project, not the town.
The 2000s miracle put a career ladder in every county. This boom puts a guard shack at every substation.
**The ladder problem**
Buried in Monday's panel -- its official title was "Small AI: More and Better Jobs," which tells you where the debate has moved, from whether to how to cushion -- was the detail that matters most to any county signing an abatement. Georgieva cited an IMF study of the American labor market. Its findings: 10 percent of jobs already require higher-level AI skills, and those jobs pay better. Routine, repetitive work is shrinking. And the low-paying jobs are increasing, in two directions -- data-center construction and related services.
Read that twice. The IMF studied the U.S. labor market and found the lower-paying job growth sitting in data centers -- the very facilities American counties are competing to pay for. The Fund's own forecast for the subsidized buildings is, almost verbatim, "lower-paying."
And that is the barbell the receipts describe from the other end: a thin, well-paid technical stratum at the top of the boom, a growing low-paid service and construction stratum at the bottom -- and, between them, the middle rungs gone. The entry-level jobs where careers used to start are precisely the ones AI eliminates first, which is why the IMF chief spent her Bangkok panel talking about baristas. The last boom distributed ladders. This one distributes a hatch and a handrail.
**What the Fund is actually warning**
Note that Georgieva's was not a robot-apocalypse speech. The U.S. study found net employment positive -- the gains are simply concentrated at the bottom of the pay scale. The panel's whole subject was diffusion: how smaller firms and poorer regions capture some of the gain instead of watching it pool. Her prescription was a homework list for governments: study the changes, rethink education, and prepare tax systems for workers who will have to reskill continuously.
Consider the irony. The IMF is telling governments to ready their tax systems for the AI age. American counties are competing to empty theirs -- sales-tax exemptions on server racks, decade-long abatements on the buildings, the electric bill rerouted to the ratepayers. The Fund is trying to argue the 2000s model into existence. Our incentive regimes are arguing the opposite.
**Where the contrivance lives**
None of this is an accounting accident. It is a design choice. The jobs number is the marketing; the incentive is the product. Announcement-day math counts construction jobs -- transient by nature, and re-counted from campus to campus as though each grand opening were the first -- plus "indirect" positions that turn out to be gas stations and motels. Payroll-day math arrives years later, after the abatements are locked in and the coverage cycle has moved on. By the time anyone audits the payroll, the subsidies are grandfathered, the company is the county's top taxpayer, and the press release has been recycled into three more groundbreakings in three more towns.
Even the Fund's growth arithmetic splits along the same seam. AI infrastructure investment, Georgieva told Reuters, is what is keeping global growth near 3 percent this year -- "despite the fact we are being dragged down by the energy supply shock." The hardware benefits accrue to the suppliers, she noted, naming Thailand. Macro, the boom is the growth story. Micro, it is the bill. The towns hosting the buildings collect the second half.
That was last month's argument, and the numbers have not aged: six in ten Americans, most Republicans included, support limiting data centers; 38 percent call them "mostly bad" against 6 percent "mostly good"; roughly half the states have seen double-digit rate hikes this year; the Ratepayer Protection Act passed the House and died in the Senate on September 30, with four Democrats in favor; and in Georgia, Ossoff's "$70 billion of your money" line outdrew anything the other side had.
An incentive sold as a jobs program when its economics are a power deal is not economic development. It is political contrivance -- the jobs were the storyboard, the electricity was the script.
After the midterms, the audit
Three weeks from today, the election settles who owns the issue. It does not change the arithmetic. Whoever wins inherits a scoreboard on which press releases finally meet payroll data. The construction peaks crest and leave; the permanent headcounts -- small, specific and disclosable -- get filed in state tax-expenditure reports that anyone with an afternoon can read. Data Center Watch already counted 120 projects, some $200 billion in investment, blocked or delayed in the first half of this year -- which means even the construction jobs are now hostage to the financing. And the Brookings Institution has begun matching the Department of Energy's data-center atlas to state incentive registries; its early read is that the incentives "may be poorly targeted," which is academic for "we paid, and it was not for the jobs."
Ribbon photographs age out of the news cycle in a week. Tax-expenditure reports do not.
Who decided?
The question that ends every ledger in this series. In the last boom, the technology went looking for people. In this one, the subsidies go looking for cheap power, and towns appear in the term sheets the way they appeared in the immigration documents -- as variables on a supply curve. Labor-supply variables then; power-supply variables now. A variable that votes.
The IMF has told us the shape of the coming work -- augmented, downgraded, eliminated; where created, lower-paid, in the buildings we are paying for; the first rung of the ladder already sawed off. The development record has told us the shape of the deal -- $2 million per permanent job, one rung per 5,000 square feet, sixteen of thirty-six states not even asking. What remains is the asking: who decided that your town was a power supply? Not the voters. Not the ratepayers. Not the county board that saw the abatement for the first time when it was a done deal.
After November 3, someone will own the electric bill. The payroll -- thin, late and finally auditable -- is the next exhibit. The jobs aren't there for the incentives. The incentives are there for the power.
Count what actually arrives.

Ribbon photographs age out of the news cycle in a week. Tax-expenditure reports do not. Who decided? The question that ends every ledger in this series. In the last boom, the technology went looking for people. In this one, the subsidies go looking for cheap power, and towns appear in the term sheets the way they appeared in the immigration documents -- as variables on a supply curve. Labor-supply variables then; power-supply variables now. A variable that votes. The IMF has told us the shape of the coming work -- augmented, downgraded, eliminated; where created, lower-paid, in the buildings we are paying for; the first rung of the ladder already sawed off. The development record has told us the shape of the deal -- $2 million per permanent job, one rung per 5,000 square feet, sixteen of thirty-six states not even asking. What remains is the asking: who decided that your town was a power supply? Not the voters. Not the ratepayers. Not the county board that saw the abatement for the first time when it was a done deal. After November 3, someone will own the electric bill. The payroll -- thin, late and finally auditable -- is the next exhibit. The jobs aren't there for the incentives. The incentives are there for the power. Count what actually arrives. ? \--- The Ledger \- Kristalina Georgieva, IMF Managing Director, IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, Bangkok, Oct 12, 2026: AI a "slow-moving tsunami"; ~40% of global jobs to be "augmented, downgraded or eliminated"; exposure ~60% in advanced economies, 23% in low-income countries; poorer nations not better off -- "just because AI is further away"; young people "first and foremost" to worry about, young graduates "first in line" (CNBC). Sources: Plataforma Media, CNBC, Citi Newsroom, Asaase Radio, Neusroom -- all Oct 12, 2026; Benzinga relay of Reuters. \- Panel's official title: "Small AI: More and Better Jobs" (World Bank live-events page). Several outlets rendered it "Small Scale AI" -- essay uses the official title. \- IMF study of the U.S. labor market, per Georgieva: ~10% of jobs already require higher-level AI skills, which pay better; routine/repetitive jobs shrinking; low-paying jobs increasing "in two directions -- data-center construction and related services" (Neusroom; Benzinga/Reuters; World Bank livestream transcript). Net employment impact positive in the area examined, gains concentrated in lower-paying jobs. The underlying study is not independently identified in available sources -- attribute as "an IMF study of the U.S. labor market," not by title. \- Georgieva quote on young workers: "Normally, they would get into these routine repetitive jobs and then grow up the ranks... I don't think any young person wants to be a barista in a coffee shop as [their] professional future." Bracketed pronoun is the outlet's rendering. Quote as relayed by Reuters/Benzinga -- original Reuters copy not independently retrieved. \- Georgieva's prescription: study labor-market changes, rethink education, prepare for continual reskilling; called for education and tax reforms (Benzinga relay; Thai Enquirer summary). \- Reuters (Oct 12, 2026): AI infrastructure investment is keeping global growth at ~3%, "despite the fact we are being dragged down by the energy supply shock"; major benefits to hardware-supplying Asian economies such as Thailand. "Energy supply shock" phrasing sourced to Reuters' report of her remarks. \- IMF Staff Note SDN/2026/001, "Bridging Skill Gaps for the Future: New Jobs Creation in the AI Age": restates 40% global exposure (60% advanced, 40% emerging; Cazzaniga et al. 2024). Note drift: the 2024 paper put low-income-country exposure at 26%; the Oct 2026 remarks say 23% -- cite the 2026 figure. \- Business Insider analysis via Good Jobs First: largest data centers generally <150 permanent workers, some 25; construction short-term (sometimes <1 yr) vs tax breaks often a decade or longer; public cost can exceed $2M per permanent FTE ≈ 8× the $262k average per job Good Jobs First found in 18 deals ≥$50M in 2023. \- Virginia JLARC (2024): typical 250,000 sq ft facility ≈ 50 full-time workers (≈1 job per 5,000 sq ft); industry employment mainly temporary construction. \- Good Jobs First: 16 of 36 state data-center subsidy programs require no job creation; most others require ≤50 jobs; New Jersey requires 100. \- Food & Water Watch (Jan 7, 2026): ~23,000 permanent data-center jobs in the U.S. as of 2024 ≈ 0.01% of U.S. employment; industry job claims "grossly inflated." \- Illinois Economic Policy Institute (via Capitol News Illinois): $57B announced investment -> 120,000+ jobs, mostly temporary; ~2,800 permanent; ≈$20.2M per permanent job. Researcher quote (Anthony Elmo, Good Jobs First): "If this were completely private money, it would be a different story." \- 2006-16 projections: total U.S. employment +10.4% vs computer-specialist occupations +25.2% (BLS-based, European Journal of Information Systems, 2008). \- Brookings, "New evidence on data center employment effects": matches DOE's Data Center Atlas to incentive registries; incentives "may be poorly targeted" -- used directionally only. \- Data Center Watch: 120 projects / ~$200B blocked or delayed, H1 2026 (carried from prior ledger). Carried from the prior ledger (Oct 2026) \- AP: ~6 in 10 Americans, including most Republicans, support limiting data centers. Pew: 38% "mostly bad" vs 6% "mostly good." Roughly half of states saw double-digit rate hikes in 2026. \- Ratepayer Protection Act: passed the House; Senate Democrats blocked it Sept 30, 2026 -- only 4 Dems (incl. Ossoff, Warnock) voted yes. \- Ossoff-Collins debate, Oct 8, 2026: $20B OpenAI campus, Effingham County; Ossoff: GOP bill "gave $70 billion of your money to data center developers." Brown-Husted (OH): Brown calls Husted "the face of data centers in Ohio." Politico (Sept 6, 2026): Dems' honed data-center message. You're currently a free subscriber to . ---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3452%2E259176%2Et0Y1lf) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3452%2E259176%2Et0Y1lf)_

When I first ran for the Minneapolis School Board, I didn’t think we would win. I thought we would stand up for our community and share important concerns.

But I never imagined how many of my neighbors shared those concerns.

While I was running, I met an old woman at a public housing complex for urban native communities.

She was selling frybread – and had a little Folgers coffee can where everyone was putting in $5. After we spoke, she took $5 out, put it in my hand, and wrapped her finger around it.

She told me: “My girl, we’re so proud of you.”

**That $5 meant more to me than a giant check from someone I knew could afford it.**

I’m running for Senate to give back to the communities that have given me so much. I want to be the voice for Minnesota families in Washington. And folks know it.

This is a grassroots campaign, powered by normal Minnesota families chipping in $5 or $10 at a time.

Since our launch, our average contribution has been just $25. Some people give more, some people give less. But I am honored and humbled by every donation. Hey Derek,

We’re now just 24 hours out from one of our last public reporting
deadlines of the entire election. And later this week, our team will

lock in through November 3rd, and the organizers we can keep in the field.
So please, rush a donation of
$25 before
midnight tomorrow to help us plan the strongest final stretch we can
afford.

the country.

in these final 16 days.

Every dollar that comes in before tomorrow night does two things at once.
It goes into the plan we’re locking this week, and it goes into the public
report our opponent and National Republicans will see.

Everything after that still gets spent — but it arrives after the
decisions are made and after the filing is read.

Dear Friend,

Please join me and an army of New Yorkers who are sick and tired of
being miserable under radical Kathy Hochul.

The choice is yours...

Safety, affordability, and freedom with a Republican governor.

High taxes, high crime, and socialism with Hochul.

It's simple. But the wrong choice will be catastrophic for New York.

We can't survive any more of Hochul's criminals first, illegals first,
socialists first, and New Yorkers LAST agenda.

I'M RUNNING FOR GOVERNOR AS THE TRUMP-ENDORSED REPUBLICAN TO FINALLY
PUT NEW YORK FIRST, BUT I CAN'T WIN WITHOUT YOUR HELP TODAY.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-w/s8kf3c5d8a8

Everything you and I have gone through in the past few years
(unaffordable prices, lawlessness, illegal alien invasion,
pro-terrorism riots, rampant social services fraud) will get 10x worse
if Hochul wins and greenlights Zohran Mamdani's Communist pipe
dream.

You know it's true because she's already doing it.

She endorsed him and paved the way for Democratic Socialists of
America (DSA) radicals to win primary elections in NYC. She gave
Mamdani a $1.5 billion bailout to fund his socialist agenda.

And in their first meeting after Mamdani won the election, they met
for over an hour to talk about how to "protect" New York from the
Trump administration.

How about Hochul protect New Yorkers from getting stabbed on the
subway? Or protect New Yorkers against the career criminals she keeps
releasing from jail? Or protect New Yorkers from violent illegal
aliens who she's helping to evade ICE deportation? Or protect New
Yorkers from fraudsters who want to rob their hard-earned taxes
blind?

She won't.

She won't protect New Yorkers like you because she's too busy
protecting herself, her Comrades in NYC, and her precious political
career.

I'm running for Governor of New York because we've got one chance to
take Hochul out of power and turn New York around, and we can't waste
it.

WILL YOU SEND YOUR BLAKEMAN FOR GOVERNOR EMERGENCY REPLY RIGHT NOW TO
JOIN MY TEAM AND HELP ME DEFEAT KATHY HOCHUL?
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-w/s8kf3c5d8a8

My name is Bruce Blakeman.

You may know me as the Republican Nassau County Executive who fought
against sanctuary policies, rejected mask mandates, stopped boys from
playing in girls' sports, hired hundreds of new police officers to
make Nassau the safest county in America, and accomplished all of that
without raising taxes by a single penny.

But today I want you to know me as the conservative who can flip New
York...

Nassau County has 110,000 more registered Democrats than Republicans,
yet I won the race for County Executive twice, winning my re-election
by a decisive 56% without compromising my values.

Many pundits see Nassau County as a demographic mirror of the state,
which means I already have a proven strategy to win.

Recent polls show that only 37% of New Yorkers want Kathy Hochul to
run for re-election, and a whopping 51% want somebody else.

SO NOT ONLY IS RADICAL KATHY HOCHUL IN THE WORST POLITICAL POSITION
SHE'S EVER BEEN IN... BUT SHE'S GOING UP AGAINST A REPUBLICAN WHO
KNOWS HOW TO WIN IN NEW YORK.

We've got the winning recipe here, but it all depends on whether or
not you join my team today.

Hochul thinks she can buy this office again. In 2022, she raised $54
million off the backs of her socialist billionaire donors... the kind
of wealthy liberals who can afford to keep illegals, career criminals,
and drug dealers out of their neighborhoods.

And on top of that, she tried to get her cronies on the New York State
Public Campaign Finance Board to deny my campaign over $7 million in
matching funds we rightfully earned!

Thankfully, the courts reinstated us and shut down her dirty political
games.

She resorted to these corrupt tactics because the polls prove that New
Yorkers are sick of her misery.

Now that it failed, imagine just how much more money she will raise
over the next three months to buy a victory she doesn't deserve.

THERE'S A REASON WHY SHE AND HER CAMPAIGN HAVE BEEN IN "PANIC MODE"
EVER SINCE I ANNOUNCED MY CANDIDACY AND RECEIVED THE ENDORSEMENT OF
PRESIDENT TRUMP...

It's because I will reverse all the damage she's done to New York:

I will hire more cops to arrest career criminals and keep them in
jail.

I will partner with ICE to deport violent illegal aliens who do
nothing but drain our resources and harm innocent New Yorkers.

I will root out all fraud in our state social programs and prosecute
fraudsters and accomplices to the fullest extent of the law.

I will protect women and children from "transgender" predators in
women's bathrooms and sports.

I will end the "Green New Scam" madness and unleash our energy
independence to immediately lower your bills.

I know this is the winning platform that all New Yorkers desperately
need... but we've got to raise enough money to run this race and fight
back against Hochul's attacks.

WILL YOU RUSH BACK YOUR BLAKEMAN FOR GOVERNOR EMERGENCY CAMPAIGN
CONTRIBUTION?
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-w/s8kf3c5d8a8

With just weeks left until the election, we don't have a minute to
waste. That's why it was worth it for me to send you this
triple-stamped return envelope today.

Any amount you can send today from $5 to $250 get us one step closer
to defeating Kathy Hochul once and for all.

The average donor gives $35 or $50. Could you give that much today?

New Yorkers have never been in a better position to win this race.

We are on the cusp of flipping New York and taking back our state. By
this time next year, New Yorkers could finally be walking our
neighborhoods without fear and paying our bills without scraping by.

And WE CAN FINALLY KICK THIS SOCIALIST SCOURGE TO THE CURB AND STOP
THE EMPIRE STATE FROM BECOMING A SOCIALIST NIGHTMARE.

Help me defeat Kathy Hochul and put New York First. Thank you for
joining me.

For New York,

Bruce Blakeman

P.S. Radical Kathy Hochul, Zohran Mamdani, and the rest of the DSA
radicals will destroy New York if we give Hochul four more years as
Governor. I'm running to defeat her because as a lifelong New Yorker
from Long Island, I refuse to let the Empire State be turned into a
socialist nightmare. Today I'm counting on you to join my team. PLEASE

| Dear Peter,

Today marks the beginning of National Estate Planning Awareness Week — a week dedicated to asking a simple but important question: if something happened to you tomorrow, are your wishes clearly documented and easy for your loved ones to carry out?

Many of us would like to answer "yes," but have never taken the time to make it official. Having a plan in place isn't just about completing the necessary paperwork; it's giving yourself and your loved ones the gift of clarity and peace of mind, knowing there will be no guesswork during an already difficult time.

A complete plan typically includes a few key documents:
* **A last will and testament,** directing how your assets are distributed
* **An advanced directive,** ensuring your healthcare wishes are honored if you are unable to speak for yourself
* **A power of attorney,** naming someone to manage your financial and/or health affairs if needed
* **Beneficiary Designations,** kept current on retirement accounts, life insurance and other payable on death assets

Long-term estate planning is also the perfect time to think about the legacy you want to leave behind. For many of the Center's supporters, that includes a commitment to protecting reproductive freedom and the belief that every person deserves the right to make decisions about their own body, health and future. A thoughtful plan is one of the most powerful ways to ensure your values continue to make a difference well beyond your lifetime.

**So we're asking: have you included the Center for Reproductive Rights in your plans?**

If you have, thank you! [We'd be honored if you'd let us know.](mailto:JStitely@reprorights.org) Sharing your intentions helps us plan for the future and gives us the chance to personally thank you for your extraordinary commitment to building, protecting and defending reproductive rights for future generations.

If you haven't yet started, or if it's been a while since you've reviewed your documents, this week is as good a time as any to do so. To help, we're offering a free [Personal Estate Planning Kit](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141677177/654369626/607887280?sourceid=1151685&utm_campaign=27emcpg-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=toolkit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyODU4YjVjYS0wOGNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_CM_JCx6S5p0XtYcdK-qlnY8FkZqx9S_9NX1wghGI2c=&emci=eed666cc-8ac9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=2858b5ca-08cb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=954237) with worksheets to help you organize your assets, wishes and important information before you meet with an attorney or advisor. | [Get Your Kit Here](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141677182/654369631/607887280?sourceid=1151685&utm_campaign=27emcpg-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=toolkit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyODU4YjVjYS0wOGNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_CM_JCx6S5p0XtYcdK-qlnY8FkZqx9S_9NX1wghGI2c=&emci=eed666cc-8ac9-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=2858b5ca-08cb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=954237)

[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkLtuhDAQRb_GdCA_eBYuIq3oNkUUKSUa7DFrxcZoMGw-PyLaH0g5Z86Mru7XfbqDD35d3iGipuwm2ieTQiKwaX-kI9gZCe0kuWxLwUvRT2CyP3GqobDaGgvCFKhFN0ilurodioeeBajaKu6cNBxrbpTC2TVuMMI2FpvC6-uf4KIXjRK8q1zTi1l2XSO6nrsWWc0hIOWKcDvm4A2sGfZvl8hgZVIsgn7kvO1MvTE5MjnuaA7C6ulXQnsZTI6nNzlRGYF-SpeoXNKJtCZicgQsTSoJDDI1HjlOezroGm4fn6No-NAPTLbXIqL1R2TqhhF8eEEDcQO_rEzd1nS-YEa6vIK03Z4-BL-3Hav5ct39Zc7_LvjU8jcAAP__CXKKyQ)

Because here's the truth most people outside our state don't realize: **_Colorado SHOULD still be a_**** _red_**** _state._** Colorado was built on independence, limited government, faith, family, and the unshakeable belief in the Second Amendment. Those values run deep in our history and in our people. But over time, the political establishment and a flood of left-wing ideas have overpowered the very values that made Colorado strong. We've watched our state shift from red, to purple, to blue -- not because the people changed, **but because leadership failed them.** _And that failure matters far beyond our borders._ Colorado has become a testing ground for policies that spread nationwide -- soft-on-crime agendas, government overreach, attacks on faith, restrictions on constitutional freedoms. **If we stop that tide**** _here_****, we stop it from sweeping across America.**

My name is Victor Marx -- a husband, father, Marine Corps veteran, former pastor, and founder of an international humanitarian organization that has carried out more than 150 high-risk rescue missions around the world. I've spent my life stepping into the chaos most people run from, fighting for those who can't fight for themselves. I never expected to run for Governor of Colorado... But people I respected deeply -- including Charlie and Erika Kirk -- believed in me and urged me to step forward because they saw what was happening here in our state. After Charlie was killed, Erika reminded me that he believed this was a fight I was meant to take on. They were right, and I am now fully committed to winning this fight. Because here's the truth most people outside our state don't realize: Colorado SHOULD still be a red state. Colorado was built on independence, limited government, faith, family, and the unshakeable belief in the Second Amendment. Those values run deep in our history and in our people. But over time, the political establishment and a flood of left-wing ideas have overpowered the very values that made Colorado strong. We've watched our state shift from red, to purple, to blue -- not because the people changed, but because leadership failed them. And that failure matters far beyond our borders. Colorado has become a testing ground for policies that spread nationwide -- soft-on-crime agendas, government overreach, attacks on faith, restrictions on constitutional freedoms. If we stop that tide here, we stop it from sweeping across America. That's why this race is so important. If Colorado flips back, the entire country will feel it. We are the top target of the MAGA movement in this country. Not one of
their targets. The top one.

Here's what's already pointed at us:

* Donald Trump's Super PAC, MAGA Inc., reserved nearly $15 million here,
then pushed it past $18 million in a week. That's more than they're
spending in any other Senate race in the country.
* Elon Musk is starting to spend here in Michigan. A trillionaire is
targeting our race.
* AIPAC is getting involved too. They nearly took us out during the
primary election.
* The Senate GOP's top Super PAC has committed $51 million to flip this
seat red. That number has ballooned over the past few weeks, and as
polling continues to tighten, we should expect it could grow even more
before Election Day.

Add it up, and Mike Rogers has over $100 million behind him. And he's on
the phone with every billionaire and corporate lobbyist he knows to pile
more on top of it.

It feels like the whole weight of the MAGA movement is pressing on our
shoulders. And in some ways, it is.

But Peter,
we have stood in front of a Goliath before, and we are still standing.

Our primary was one of the most expensive Democratic Senate primaries in
the country's history. We got outspent 11 to 1 and still won.

We won because people gave $10 and $15 at a time to emails exactly like
this one.

During the primary, it took nearly everything in us to overcome the big
money forces, and now we have to do it again with less time. We have just

Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

clean_body: Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance | | | | | | | Patriot, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. Patriot, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece. JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like. Friend,
We'll be blunt: three major stories just broke in Florida's U.S. Senate race – a must-win to hold the Senate majority. **And they 've got us on edge.**
1\. A new poll has Senator Ashley Moody at 47% and democratic socialist Angie Nixon at 45%. Two points. Inside the margin of error.
**2\. Nixon just OUTRAISED Senator Moody last quarter.**
3\. Bernie Sanders is pouring his $23M war chest into Florida to drag her over the finish line.
Any one of these would be a warning sign. **All three at once? That 's how a political earthquake starts.**
Last month, the same pollster had it 45.2% to 44.8%. Before that, another poll had it dead even, 47–47. Each one calls Florida's U.S. Senate race a coin flip.
Sure, we could make ourselves feel better by pointing to other polls with Senator Moody further ahead. But pollsters wrote Nixon off in her primary too. She was outraised 16 to 1 – and still won by 12 points. Now she's got real money behind her. The Left's money machine is lining up, and Bernie's coming with it.
Bernie is going all in. He's flooding Florida with organizers and texts. And he's here in person, rallying with her across the state.
We've watched Bernie do this before. AOC got her start organizing for his 2016 campaign – now she's the face of the radical Left. He went all in for Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist – and Mamdani is now running New York City. He's backing hard-left Senate candidates in Michigan, Minnesota and Maine. And now he's added Florida to his list.
Nixon is exactly Bernie's kind of candidate. She's a member of the Democratic Socialists of America. She worked on his 2016 campaign. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. And she was one of only 7 members of the Florida House to vote against teaching the history of communism in our schools.
We're rapidly running out of time to stave off this political earthquake. Floridians are already casting their ballots right now, and every vote that's cast is one we can't win back.
So let's be crystal clear about what happens next: **if Florida falls, the Senate falls with it.** Republicans lose the majority. Chuck Schumer takes back control. President Trump's agenda is dead on arrival, and the radical Left gets two years of investigations and obstruction.
**We cannot let that happen.**
She's never had this kind of money before. Bernie's money is already moving. Friend, When you think about the _kids growing up across Tennessee,_ whether they’re sitting in an overcrowded, under-resourced classrooms, growing up in the shadow of a polluting data center, or hoping to one day afford a home and to start a family of their own in the hometown they love, _you realize what this election is really all about._ _**It’s about _their_ future**._ **Every policy we are fighting for in this campaign comes down to one simple question:** _What kind of Tennessee are we leaving to the next generation?_ When we talk about fully funding our public schools and stopping voucher scams, we are fighting to make sure every child has a world-class education and every opportunity to succeed, right in their own neighborhood, no matter their zip code. When we talk about _**expanding healthcare, lowering the cost of living, eliminating the grocery tax, and wiping out crushing medical debt,**_ we are fighting to lift the financial weight off working parents so they can actually build a stable, secure home and still have time to spend with their kids. And when we talk about _**protecting our natural resources, standing up to corporate special interests, and restoring common-sense leadership,**_ we are fighting to ensure our children inherit a Tennessee that works for them, not out-of-state billionaires.

We are in _the final stretch of this campaign,_ and _**early voting is happening right now through October 29th**_. The decisions we make in this will shape the future of Tennessee for decades to come. One day our kids will look back and _they will know what we did in this critical and decisive moment._

body:
But Scott needs all the help he can get to break the GOP chokehold on his state.
Hi, Peter – I'm reaching out today because now more than ever, _Mississippi Matters._ Here's what you need to know:

If Democrats want to take back the Senate majority, we’ve got to FIGHT for every pick-up opportunity on the map this cycle, not just the evergreen battlegrounds.
---
Between the national environment and the growing grassroots momentum behind his groundbreaking campaign, **Democratic nominee Scott Colom has a real shot at delivering GOP Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith a shocking defeat.**
**With the second-highest poverty rate and lowest life expectancy of the 50 states, Scott's surging because voters in MS are hungry for _real change._** And his campaign focused on raising wages, lowering costs, and saving health care is giving folks in the Magnolia State real hope. But Scott needs all the help he can get to break the GOP chokehold on Mississippi.
So when he reached out to me for help, the best way I could was by passing along his message, in his own words, to top grassroots supporters like you.
**_[Please split a donation between me and Scott's campaign now to help him show the country just how much Mississippi Matters when he flips this seat blue on Election Day.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141682765/654390260/319314721?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk727-bu-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4M2MzYmM1OS0xNWNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ceCrVG_P4fX8-81hf6Xz149j2eSoP4dM3kqGAuZMq6Y=)_**
And now, I'll let him take it from here – thank you.

Patty Murray

From: **Scott Colom**
Subject: A miracle is brewing in Mississippi
---
| | |
---
I’ll get right to it, Peter: _**New polling was just released and it shows that we’re tied with Cindy Hyde-Smith. A miracle is brewing in Mississippi.**_
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141682766/654390261/319314721?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk727-bu-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4M2MzYmM1OS0xNWNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ceCrVG_P4fX8-81hf6Xz149j2eSoP4dM3kqGAuZMq6Y=)
Our first poll after we launched had us down 13 points. Then the next had us down 3. **Now we’ve closed the gap and are tied with Cindy Hyde-Smith. Mississippi’s Senate race is winnable.**
| | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141682767/654390262/319314721?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk727-bu-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4M2MzYmM1OS0xNWNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ceCrVG_P4fX8-81hf6Xz149j2eSoP4dM3kqGAuZMq6Y=)
---
Everywhere I go, everybody knows why I’m running: Higher wages. Lower costs. Save our health care and save our hospitals.
But Cindy Hyde-Smith? Nobody knows what she’s running for. She hasn’t spoken to voters at a town hall in six years.
Mississippi is ready for a senator that’ll fight for them, not their special interests.
While momentum is on our side, please don’t think that we’re overconfident. We know full well that this is going to be a tough race. **Cindy has a massive fundraising advantage over us, and is fully backed by the D.C. swamp establishment.**
Now, here’s the thing: This poll isn’t worth a hill of beans if we aren’t able to get our message out to voters during the final sprint to November. That’s where you come in.
This is a grassroots campaign – while Cindy Hyde-Smith has billionaires, we’re powered by everyday Mississippians, chipping in $5 or $10 when they can.
**[The only way we’re going to be able to put out a strong report that shows us on track to flip this seat is with your help. So, if you can, please split a donation between my campaign and Patty Murray's campaign today!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141682768/654390263/319314721?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk727-bu-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4M2MzYmM1OS0xNWNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ceCrVG_P4fX8-81hf6Xz149j2eSoP4dM3kqGAuZMq6Y=)**

**I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

clean_body: Then I went public.| | | | = I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents. I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home. I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country. After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents. Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser. I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first. Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors. I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country. Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump? For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening. But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question: Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous? In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public. I was terrified. I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence. But silence costs more. So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat. Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue. I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first. Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences. That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild. Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him. They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts. It MUST reach the ballot box. It MUST be organized. And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power. = | | | = MAGA wants us exhausted. They want every new outrage to make us feel a little more powerless. They want us to believe that one person speaking out, casting a ballot or making a contribution cannot possibly change anything. I learned the opposite. I learned that courage is contagious. Control of Congress could come down to only a handful of seats. Your contribution can help elect Democrats who will defend our Constitution, demand accountability and finally place a meaningful check on Trump’s unfettered power. Please help Resist Reclaim Rebuild fight for those victories today. = Stay informed. Stay compassionate. Stay hopeful. But above all, refuse to be silent. He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. **Now he's fighting for his own freedom** – [**and he needs your help.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMzMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA5nFzFjx6OYgMaAPmz_frtpUbhAxmNp9yEFDkNN2K4Io08RzoGU052pNMz97tcatFEST53IgCHliu6_ehYAxdIOYvT_plP8rqENHyKwzMg) All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx.

| | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled. Duran had only moments to react. He didn't reach for his firearm. He didn't use deadly force. **Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him.** The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries. Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison. And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away. [**Will you help Sgt. Duran fight for his freedom?**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMzMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA5nFzFj0UaI0uIHiiNcaAEoM5H48bYN_piuvSxpjwTiv9_Sj5jbge5juu-dVvuvrpBafWFd_Vdu6g8-EzxU6iGM63SJZSEBm5TwZxXG9XQ) The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. Duran and helping fund his appeal. But legal battles like this are long, difficult, and incredibly expensive. And while Erik fights for his freedom, his wife and children are left carrying the burden alongside him. **They’re not only facing the reality of their husband and father spending the next 9 years in prison.** **Their own lives have been threatened because of this case.** That's why I’m asking for your help today. **[Please make a tax-deductible donation of $35, $50, $100, or more to help fund Sgt. Duran's appeal and give him the resources he needs to fight for his freedom.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMzMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA5nFzFj1LEue2OACmW0Xtm8WXoGQHx2vT5Y8_rmFxqvMwe4jYeaAkDiA07a7Tej0Kz5KQaef075srt0yRfi0ZVqeYxPbmbl5XlGlyXAXqw)** **_Erik spent 15 years protecting others._** **_Now he needs people like you standing behind him.[Every donation makes a difference.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMzMsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA5nFzFj2uSxo30w4Y0nxv6cw8-c658izBu93F5TTRVC0skGSveYXIsBmMrqAD6LbYMuzH20GzM07v2Kqo_A_5jWIlqPBwJk4780KTSL8qA)_** **_Thank you for standing with Sgt. Duran._** Sincerely,

| | | **Jason Johnson, President** _**
Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund**_

Fellow Patriot,

Early voting for the General Election starts this MONDAY here in South Carolina.

Democrats have made it clear: **they want to flip South Carolina in November.** Liberal Annie Andrews is spending MILLIONS of dollars across our state to make that happen. Her allies are betting that conservatives will wait until Election Day while they bank their votes early.

We can't let that happen. So I'm asking for two favors, Fellow Patriot.

> _**FIRST:**_ If you live in South Carolina, bank your vote early. Starting Monday, get out and vote, then bring your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers. Hi friend, I wanted to reach out and say thank you for supporting my campaign. | Friends, Did you see the news? Democrat State Senate Candidate Cecil Abels of Rochester**** was **forced to suspend his campaign** due to the fact that he did not meet residency requirements to be a member of the Senate. This begs the question, **why can’t the Senate Democrats find candidates that are actually _from_ New Hampshire to run? ** Lets do a run down: In District 7, Rebecca Harned has unquestionable ties to the DC Beltway and at least one more home in Colorado. She works for an NGO based out of Maryland and authored a blog about her love affair for living in DC. She even signed a mortgage document in 2025 that specifically references a “primary residence” in Virginia. Meanwhile, in District 18, Leonard Bell has a mysterious second life in New Brunswick, Canada that he still has yet to explain. Peter,
Here’s the situation: We’re still coming up short of our $1 million rapid response goal in anticipation of President Trump’s rally here in North Carolina next week. This is a goal we have to hit to respond to the president’s lies and keep up our momentum in the final weeks of this race.

[**_Will you chip in $2 right now to help us reach our critical goal before Trump takes the stage, flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19983?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1716&t=8&akid=4642%2E124072%2ECGDDb_)

$2 because North Carolina is the best chance for Democrats to flip a Republican-held Senate seat in the country.
$2 because if we lose here, we’ll lose our shot at taking back the majority.
$2 because GOP dark-money super PACs have invested millions into false attack ads against me.
$2 because we can make life better for working people, put an end to the chaos and stop President Trump’s cruel agenda – but only if we come together.

Peter, I’m sorry to be so blunt, but with President Trump coming back to North Carolina yet again in just a couple days for _another_ MAGA rally, I have to ask:
[**_Will you chip in $5 to ensure we’re ready for whatever attacks he throws my way?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1694&amount=5&t=8&akid=4690%2E124072%2EhZl6Fh)
Let me explain why your support is so important – and what could happen without it.
1\. Trump was just here last month. He’s coming to NC again to rally alongside my MAGA opponent, Michael Whatley, and rile up the GOP base right before the election. And we’ve just learned JD Vance will be here _tomorrow_ – to do exactly the same thing.
2\. North Carolinians are already voting. If we don’t have the resources to fight back against Trump and the GOP’s oncoming wave of attacks, their lies and distortions could be the last thing people hear before heading to the polls.
3\. I just set a goal to raise $1,000,000 before Trump’s big rally, and I need your help to reach it. Falling short would mean putting our chances of flipping this seat at risk – so we simply cannot let that happen.
**Thousands of grassroots supporters are chipping in today to fuel this movement. Now, I’m asking you to join them. Please, Peter:**
[**_Will you give $5 or whatever you can today to help us reach our crucial $1 million goal, win in North Carolina and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1694&amount=5&t=9&akid=4690%2E124072%2EhZl6Fh)
