This will make your blood boil.
#
Peter —
Last night, JD Vance was confronted by the husband of a soldier killed in Iran. His answer was an utter embarrassment.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-oct26.xXsDMU&refcode=em261018-2-180&t=1&akid=35723%2E3013755%2EESz-P4)
We are eight months into Donald Trump’s illegal war with Iran, and it is an abject failure.
They’re covering up the casualties — 21 U.S. service members dead and more than 800 others wounded. They went to war without adequate force protections which got those Troops wounded and killed. They’re hiding the damage at American bases. And eight months in, they still have no plan for ending this war.
**The Vice President of the United States, a veteran, knows this. So he is either ignorant of the issues that have been reported, or lying to this Gold Star husband’s face.**
It’s clear that Trump, Vance, and the GOP don’t give a shit. They will continue their Forever War and put more lives in danger if we don’t win back control of Congress.
This all stops if we do.

subject: Peter, this won't make the news
body:
Our Dream Lab graduates went home and organized. Here's what they told us. | | | Peter, Nine people at a pickup soccer game. Eight around a card table. Ten painting little pots with things that remind them of home. None of it will make the news. That's the point. This summer, I wrote to you about immigrant youth leaders who spent six weeks in **Level Up: The Dream Lab** learning how to organize. This fall, they went home and did it. They booked spaces, made flyers, brought food, and waited to see who would walk through the door. **[Every conversation, every connection, and every new face builds community, resilience, and power. One new organizer said it was their first event ever: _"I felt exhausted after the event but felt satisfied that people came and enjoyed it."_
Another pushed through permits and red tape to pull off a field day. Fewer people came than they'd hoped. Their next step is already in motion: finding a new space to bring it back.
And one wrote that their next step is to _"continue being loud about my status and continue to love people in such a way that inspires them to also take action."_
This is the unglamorous, critical work of movement building. _When we build spaces rooted in culture and belonging, people don’t just show up — they stay, they organize, and they lead._ Every room these organizers filled is a place where neighbors met, laughed, and learned they aren't alone.
**That's how power gets built: one conversation at a time, by people who keep showing up.**

clean_body: Our Dream Lab graduates went home and organized. Here's what they told us. | | | Peter, Nine people at a pickup soccer game. Eight around a card table. Ten painting little pots with things that remind them of home. None of it will make the news. That's the point. This summer, I wrote to you about immigrant youth leaders who spent six weeks in Level Up: The Dream Lab learning how to organize. This fall, they went home and did it. They booked spaces, made flyers, brought food, and waited to see who would walk through the door. | | One new organizer said it was their first event ever: "I felt exhausted after the event but felt satisfied that people came and enjoyed it." Another pushed through permits and red tape to pull off a field day. Fewer people came than they'd hoped. Their next step is already in motion: finding a new space to bring it back. And one wrote that their next step is to "continue being loud about my status and continue to love people in such a way that inspires them to also take action." This is the unglamorous, critical work of movement building. When we build spaces rooted in culture and belonging, people don’t just show up — they stay, they organize, and they lead. Every room these organizers filled is a place where neighbors met, laughed, and learned they aren't alone. That's how power gets built: one conversation at a time, by people who keep showing up. subject: Tell Congress to put our communities before Big Tech
body:
An emergency power order is another warning about unchecked data center expansion. | |
---
Peter, **We all depend on reliable electricity to keep our homes safe, our schools running, and our neighborhoods connected. But as tech corporations race to build more data centers, our communities are being asked to shoulder the costs of their enormous appetite for power.** This week, the Energy Department authorized emergency backup power measures for the regional grid that serves Pennsylvania and millions of our neighbors. If needed, the grid operator can direct data centers and other large electricity users to switch to backup generators, including generators that burn diesel. Above-average heat and power plant maintenance prompted the order. But the massive growth in electricity demand from data centers is adding pressure to a grid that our families already rely on. Now, emergency fossil fuel backups are among the tools available to keep that system running. **We deserve a say before corporations push our electric grid further, drive up costs, and put more pollution into our neighborhoods. That’s why we’re taking this demand to Congress.** [**Tell Congress to support a moratorium on new data centers until protections for our communities are in place.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxhjG7-DrcPdCmyOmMJZYw6jmiWm5sGrmjqK5u8wmap3PzN2RNa4pbwd9YfydoQeEsT2uxZk3bl_5YcZFZ9F04v6iVjQdxQ5CY8EXaiHahvVXDhFieXREoeDGVoWWQoiun-TupO0AHvEG4BliGot2-dAoOs8MN5s8nMMv9_LQBEWDoJnTdYXTZOosYdTt7jvA06vm5Se8vhLxHOj_53xcXdIur5uuA-A81FeuQpSCyPeHTsFfHbcWbxfc2-5b6ZCkkSnBpDHkuCm8pmjFNyWI2EgJLFrolAplBqMgWaLBfS5BBsxJ4zS1gb6mhCBLyjauiIj819yD_EWTn10woaJz3_d0UFbIkgHX92cjyo0_pdaE257UVTpaHCwyrrIE-c1BORWaDFovEedYDdR3XEBtKk-URw4W3W7xEl2SF0NcVXdKl8rMyr0LdOpQVYLbYABFl/4uz/D8bfqUA_QpqSgy9XPE86Jg/h0/h001.srSgqmZSApcyRhWGv0s8geFn5vKmVLPI6hQK36L2MtA) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxhjG7-DrcPdCmyOmMJZYw6jmiWm5sGrmjqK5u8wmap3PzN2RNa4pbwd9YfydoQeEsT2uxZk3bl_5YcZFZ9F04v6iVjQdxQ5CY8EXaiHahvVXDhFieXREoeDGVoWWQoiun-TupO0AHvEG4BliGot2-dAoOs8MN5s8nMMv9_LQBEWDoJnTdYXTZOosYdTt7jvA0JTG1BF_pe3CLXTO2iMazkbdTnfZKv4ZlVp0wJDJQk8d4VkQ88nxDU9S1mQQ9s9lksA3O7bsvgAZFpmdkKsQf_uji0HGwI8sktfKUAi_iaSev2Od6zZceXlQoo7WBJFc-gMj8uKGD-jGCjqq9tRmr6Pu-DfclkacDU6P-03RzFj2Hb2QJjEN1R8uSC0ipvWFWt8IiM1iaS3-LApn914x7ofbvCMYim--Q9iSBtUECE8nLDwZiPr1-XjFgE72JUIPt/4uz/D8bfqUA_QpqSgy9XPE86Jg/h1/h001.Tf0-dwnuNbbIjB7rzn0kRPfHybgSDi1f_Kwt2UOr_vs)

**At OnePA, we organize because working-class communities deserve the power to shape the decisions impacting our lives.** That includes who uses our water, who pays for new energy infrastructure, and whose health gets sacrificed when corporate expansion comes first.
We know Black and working-class neighborhoods have carried the burden of corporate pollution for generations. We have every reason to demand enforceable protections before another industry locks our communities into more pollution and higher costs.
Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez are calling for a pause on new data centers until public safeguards are in place. As opposition to unchecked expansion crosses party lines, we have an opening to turn community demands into action in Congress.
**We can build on that momentum by organizing our neighbors and making sure our representatives hear us again. Our communities deserve affordable power, clean water, and a real voice in what gets built around us.**
[**Send a message to Congress today. Pause the data center boom and put our communities’ health, resources, and economic security first.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxhjG7-DrcPdCmyOmMJZYw6jmiWm5sGrmjqK5u8wmap3PzN2RNa4pbwd9YfydoQeEsT2uxZk3bl_5YcZFZ9F04v6iVjQdxQ5CY8EXaiHahvVXDhFieXREoeDGVoWWQoiun-TupO0AHvEG4BliGot2-dAoOs8MN5s8nMMv9_LQBEWDoJnTdYXTZOosYdTt7jvA03Vv9qOK6vQ1NcU43UKY8RvzbgU3zR4g7okZU6UgByBccoDX8B7ijykifmq4SMxyQwAPcYudKSsRpC4kL2lGX2eceoj_a-93cG9EX1v1TJGSXprJyYzbnitRLlZ5JmG61LHCpoXAWjCqmLRnt5tDFksj2m26Bbe8gvOZkMinKJWorCmFl0FiIuVQ5T-9UD4ed_v2hPTcqtVpkf6M-IeN8QCDBuQqGhhZ-WklM4EdMTCxkmokz1eYg6gL4VQo6ZHHo/4uz/D8bfqUA_QpqSgy9XPE86Jg/h2/h001.Gc8KhKTYVzufW2CF_L5FvDi7P0Iiq0dJBfCtAL7HV6k)

Tomorrow is a word that holds deep meaning to me right now.
**_Tomorrow_** stands for a Texas where families come before data centers when it comes to clean drinking water.
**_Tomorrow_** stands for fully-funded public schools and a lieutenant governor's office that will never let a voucher scheme raid those funds again.
**_Tomorrow_** stands for real property tax relief, so that Texans who have spent decades building a life in this state don't get taxed out of the homes they worked for.
**_Tomorrow_** stands for doctors practicing medicine without fear. Childcare that families can afford. Rents that don't squeeze working Texans out of the cities they built.
**_Tomorrow_** stands for a Texas Senate led by someone who has never once sold her vote to the highest bidder.
Dan Patrick had a decade of tomorrows to work for Texans. He spent them fighting for his billionaire donors. He spent them setting up a voucher system that defunds your kids' schools to pay for someone else's private tuition. He spent them making sure the wealthiest Texans never have to wait in line with the rest of us.
**_On November 3, his “tomorrows” as Lt. Governor are over._**
[**Every dollar you send tonight is a vote for a different kind of Texas. It pays for the last days of ads, the final round of calls, the organizers holding the line until polls close.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141691289/654411848/-1125811855?refcode=du_em_101826_tomorrow&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGUxYzdlZjItMjdjYi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=QY9yJBwQE0o_HGxuwr7fswAj31-QPL2ZPkueQFWtGiE=)
_Tomorrow starts tonight._
Let's go win it.
Rep. Vikki Goodwin

AI Is Running Out of Power. Part of the Answer May Be Three Miles Under the Utah Desert.
AI data centers are straining America’s power supply, and tech giants are signing electricity deals years in advance. In a remote corner of Utah, a small crew now drills nearly three miles into the Earth in about two weeks. What’s down there is starting to get very serious attention.

AI data centers are straining America’s power supply, and tech giants are signing electricity deals years in advance. In a remote corner of Utah, a small crew now drills nearly three miles into the Earth in about two weeks. What’s down there is starting to get very serious attention. Threat level 3/5 — Guarded | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|--- | From the highway, it doesn’t look like much: a few drilling rigs in the desert of southwestern Utah, far from any big city. The evidence board | | Why the Desert Matters ---|--- | EVIDENCE Exhibit A — the hunger. A single AI supercomputer, Colossus 1 in Memphis, draws more than 300 megawatts. body:
Hey Peter, I know it's late. I should definitely be asleep by now, but I can’t stop running these numbers through my head:
1. MAGA Republicans are on track to spend more than **$100 million** on ads in this race. They’ve reserved over $1 million a day in ads from now until Election Day. That equates to seeing pro-Rogers and anti-us ads on nearly every commercial break and every phone screen across Michigan.

1. AIPAC money is flooding into Michigan _again._ AIPAC and allied groups already spent **tens of millions** against this campaign. We made it through the primary, but this fight isn't over, and they aren't giving up yet.

1. **More than half** of our state’s voters cast their ballots before Election Day. That means we can’t wait until the last few days of this race to reach them. It’ll already be too late by then.

That’s what’s keeping me up. Because what happens next comes down to one question: do we have enough grassroots support to stay on the air, answer every attack, and reach voters while they’re still filling out their ballots?
Peter, I’ve put my faith in this team since day one, and you’ve never let me down. I know I’ve asked a lot. But with less than three weeks left and ballots already being cast, I have to ask again:
**_Can you chip in $5 or any amount right now so we can keep our ads running while Michiganders are voting?_**

Elon Musk Built One of the World’s Biggest AI Supercomputers in 122 Days. Then He Rented Out All of It.
Colossus 1 in Memphis holds about 220,000 Nvidia chips and draws more than 300 megawatts. In May, its entire capacity went to a single outside tenant, one Musk had been publicly criticizing for months. Who would make that deal, and why, says a lot about where AI is heading.

Elon Musk doesn’t usually share. So when the whole of one of his AI supercomputers was handed over to someone else this spring, people in the industry noticed. Most investors didn’t. They should have, because the deal explains how scarce computing power has become.
The evidence board
| | What We Know
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the machine.** Colossus 1 was built in South Memphis in just 122 days and went live in 2024. It now holds roughly 220,000 Nvidia processors.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the deal.** On May 6, 2026, the entire capacity of Colossus 1, more than 300 megawatts, was leased to one tenant. Musk said his own AI training had already moved to a larger cluster, Colossus 2.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the empire.** Earlier this year SpaceX merged with Musk’s AI company. In June, SpaceX went public and ended its first trading day worth about $2.1 trillion.
| OUR THEORY
---
When competitors start renting computing power from each other, it tells you that compute has become the scarcest resource in technology. Whoever owns it holds the leverage, and whoever needs it pays. That shift is reshaping who wins the AI race.

| | The Bottleneck Inside the Data Center
---|---
Hundreds of thousands of chips are only useful if they can talk to each other fast enough, and copper wiring is running into physical limits. So the industry is turning to light. In July, Nvidia began shipping its first switches with optics built directly into the chip package to select partners, and Broadcom’s version entered volume production.
Research firm TrendForce expects this market to ramp up in earnest in 2027 and 2028.

Hello -
My name is Mary Peltola, and with just a few weeks until Election Day, I want to share with you why I made the decision to run for this Senate seat – and to ask for your support in this final stretch.
**[But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Michael Bennet's Victory Fund, The Colorado Way:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141691738/654413289/-874769866?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1620-bu-d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMWU3MThiOC0yYmNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hg8Ykktasv-QGZTbtXBnPaAWxWmvuPlBxDkBUOQLMac=)**

---
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**
So I am asking:
**[Please split a contribution between The Colorado Way and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today. We are looking for a huge surge in support to put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast to give us the resources we need to WIN in November. ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141691740/654413291/-874769866?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1620-bu-d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMWU3MThiOC0yYmNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hg8Ykktasv-QGZTbtXBnPaAWxWmvuPlBxDkBUOQLMac=)**

clean_body: | | | = Hello - My name is Mary Peltola, and with just a few weeks until Election Day, I want to share with you why I made the decision to run for this Senate seat – and to ask for your support in this final stretch. = | | = Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets – not ours. And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest. It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted. I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home. My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption. I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future. This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/a1f3bafa-9003-4061-9f75-5714e64375b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

I'm excited to officially kick off our **One Fight Tour**. We'll be traveling across Texas to meet with voters, talk about what's at stake in this election, and make sure Texans are ready to cast their ballots.
Since launching this campaign, I've traveled thousands of miles across our great state, meeting thousands of Texans who feel like they've been left behind by Greg Abbott. I've heard the same thing over and over again: **Texans are working harder than ever, but getting less in return.**
That's why I'm running for Governor.
For too long, Greg Abbott has put the interests of his billionaire donors ahead of hardworking Texas families. Our neighborhood schools are struggling, everyday costs are soaring, and the American Dream is slipping further out of reach.
But everywhere I've traveled, I've met Texans who believe, just like I do, that it's time for change.
**And now, with multiple independent polls showing us ahead of Greg Abbott, we 're closer than ever to making that vision a reality.**
Over the next few weeks, we're taking that momentum on the road with one message: **There 's only One Fight this November -- will Texas be a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaires' world and we just live here?**
I'm fighting to make sure we realize the vision of Texas where we all have a seat at the table and the rich and powerful don't get to dictate how the rest of us live. I'm going on our One Fight Tour with that message, and I'm hoping you can join me.
Here's where you can find us:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a1f3bafa-9003-4061-9f75-5714e64375b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**[RSVP to a stop in your city and make sure to check back for more cities we'll be adding!](https://substack.com/redirect/a1f3bafa-9003-4061-9f75-5714e64375b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
We're going to secure the American Dream by saving our neighborhood schools and putting money back in Texans' pockets.
But none of that happens unless we show up and vote.
**Early voting begins October 19, and Election Day is November 3.** Make your plan to vote, remind your friends and family, and help us spread the word in every corner of Texas.
[FIND YOUR VOTING INFORMATION ->](https://substack.com/redirect/be3de8e9-e502-4d9b-b504-f95dcdb67b2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We've come so far, but we are not done yet. With just weeks left until Election Day, every conversation, every door knocked, and every vote will make a difference.
Texans are ready for change, and this November, with your support, we're going to make it happen.
Let's go win this thing!
Gina
**[P.S. Our One Fight Tour is about turning the momentum we've built into a victory on November 3rd. If you can, will you chip in to help us reach more Texas voters in these final few 16 days?](https://substack.com/redirect/0ed15124-022e-46f0-8018-3a99cccf1d3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. Derek, Republicans
made a bet on Pennsylvania.

Friend, I was in a crowded coffee shop in Topeka a few weeks ago listening to Kansans talk about their challenges, dreams and hopes for the future.

While I was there, I shared the most fundamental message of my campaign: **Remember to be a good neighbor.** You don’t have to agree with someone to love them. In fact, our system works best when we disagree, because then we can find a compromise that addresses the concerns of both sides.

Early voting has started in North Carolina, and I’m feeling hopeful.
I know you’re getting a lot of messages right now, so thank you for opening my email and staying engaged. I appreciate it.
Here's the thing: The GOP knows our grassroots movement has the momentum – so they’re doubling down on their attacks. body:
We turned a long shot into a dead heat. Now we need to finish it.
**A new poll just came out showing me ahead of Greg Abbott, 47% to 45%.
**
That’s the fifth poll in the last month to show us leading this race. Not tied. Ahead.
If you’d told me a year ago, when we launched this campaign, that we’d be here, I’m not sure I would have believed you. But here we are, and it’s because of people like you.
**[So I’m asking: will you split $5 between Aaron Ford and my campaign today to keep this momentum going?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261018_3_ak.iGiYh1&amount=5&refcode=em20261018-1099&t=2&akid=1117%2E127862%2ECBRyA1)**
Here’s what the numbers tell me:
Texans know Greg Abbott, and they’re tired of him. 52% of likely voters view him unfavorably, and only 44% favorably. **After more than a decade of corruption that’s left Texas families to fend for themselves, voters across the political spectrum are ready for change.**
And the more Texans get to know me, the more they like what they see. My name ID has jumped to 79% in just the last few weeks, and I’m still viewed favorably by a 12-point margin (45% to 33%), even after Abbott has spent millions attacking me.
Grassroots donations from supporters like you made that possible. **[Will you make a donation split between Aaron Ford and my campaign so we can reach the voters who still don’t know me?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261018_3_ak.iGiYh1&amount=5&refcode=em20261018-1099&t=3&akid=1117%2E127862%2ECBRyA1)**
Together, we’ve turned this race from a long shot into a dead heat. A few months ago, people said we’d never get this close to taking Texas back. Now we’re on the edge of making history.
But Abbott knows it too. He’s raised more than $141 million in this campaign and already spent over $120 million of it trying to stop us. He still has $17 million left to spend on false attack ads right as voting begins. **The undecided voters who will decide this race are about to be buried in them, and we need to make sure they hear from us too.**
Now is the time for your donation to have the largest impact. **[Can you make a donation split between Aaron Ford and my campaign before early voting starts so we can stay on the air in the final weeks?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261018_3_ak.iGiYh1&amount=5&refcode=em20261018-1099&t=4&akid=1117%2E127862%2ECBRyA1)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261018_3_ak.iGiYh1&amount=5&refcode=em20261018-1099&t=23&akid=1117%2E127862%2ECBRyA1)**
Thank you,
Gina

name: Scott Colom
subject: These opportunities don’t come around every year
body:
It’s Scott
Colom. Please don’t skip past this important email.

The polls are tied.
Ratings experts just upgraded this race in our direction.
We are on the verge of flipping Mississippi’s Senate seat blue.

There’s just one problem: Republicans are massively outspending us in the
final stretch.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261018_3.C_weXp&refcode=em20261018-3&t=1001&akid=9580%2E582294%2ElJcBJa ]Politico: Democrats spy a red-state opening. There may not be enough cash for
it.

Cindy Hyde-Smith has put major money behind lies and smears attacking me.

She has millions of dollars to spend on those lies, thanks to all the
corporate PACs and billionaires who have bankrolled her campaign.

My campaign isn’t like that. We’ve turned this Safe Republican seat into a
real battleground, thanks to the support of ordinary people chipping in $5
or $10 at a time. I’m incredibly proud of that, and I hope you are too.

But it means that we’re relying on emails like this one to make sure we
have the resources to close out the final stretch.

Please know. When you see me and my team out there, fighting for
votes–we’re only able to be out there thanks to the generous help of
people like you.

This is our best chance to flip Mississippi in a generation. Opportunities
like this don’t come around every year.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261018_3.C_weXp&refcode=em20261018-3&t=1002&akid=9580%2E582294%2ElJcBJa ]So today I’m humbly asking: Can you split a donation between my
campaign and Chris Pappas to make sure we have the resources to close out
the next 16 days? In a race this close, anything you can give makes a
major difference.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261018_3.C_weXp&amount=5&refcode=em20261018-3&t=1021&akid=9580%2E582294%2ElJcBJa ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Scott Colom

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9580%2E582294%2ElJcBJa

These photos come from the EPIC mosque forum, the McKinney PTA forum, the Allen Community forum, and the Divine 9 forum.
Zero Republicans attended any of them.
One of those forums met at the retirement community where Keith Self’s own brother lives. He skipped that one, too.
Our Constitution promises something specific when it calls this a representative democracy.
The word “representative” is a job description.
The deal struck at this country’s founding says power flows up from the people, and the people who hold it must stand before their neighbors, face the hard questions, and answer for their record.
No title or bad legislative year exempts a politician from that deal.
Perhaps nobody explained that to Keith Self, who went on national television this month and declared this district’s place in Congress “my seat.”

Keith Self and his fellow extremists spend all day shouting that democracy is under attack.
They invent enemies in every mosque and immigrant neighborhood.
And they cast themselves as our country’s last line of defense.
Then democracy convenes in a church hall or a community center and asks them to participate, and they are nowhere to be found.
You cannot claim to defend democracy when you refuse to participate in it.
Democracy survives on citizens gathering in rooms like the ones in these photos, and Republicans like my opponent keep ducking the room.
Our movement keeps showing up because the people of this district are owed answers for years of Keith Self’s and Donald Trump’s failures, from the gas pump to the grocery store to the war nobody voted for.
And we keep showing up because every forum reminds us who this seat belongs to.
Seniors, parents, veterans, worshippers, neighbors.

clean_body: Empty Republican chairs at four straight forums. | | Peter, For months I've been running into the same scene, all across this district: A community organizes a candidate forum. Every candidate on the ballot gets an invitation. Then the Democrats show up, and the Republican chairs stand empty. | These photos come from the EPIC mosque forum, the McKinney PTA forum, the Allen Community forum, and the Divine 9 forum. Zero Republicans attended any of them. One of those forums met at the retirement community where Keith Self’s own brother lives. He skipped that one, too. Our Constitution promises something specific when it calls this a representative democracy. The word “representative” is a job description. The deal struck at this country’s founding says power flows up from the people, and the people who hold it must stand before their neighbors, face the hard questions, and answer for their record. No title or bad legislative year exempts a politician from that deal. Perhaps nobody explained that to Keith Self, who went on national television this month and declared this district’s place in Congress “my seat.” | Keith Self and his fellow extremists spend all day shouting that democracy is under attack. They invent enemies in every mosque and immigrant neighborhood. And they cast themselves as our country’s last line of defense. Then democracy convenes in a church hall or a community center and asks them to participate, and they are nowhere to be found. You cannot claim to defend democracy when you refuse to participate in it. Democracy survives on citizens gathering in rooms like the ones in these photos, and Republicans like my opponent keep ducking the room. Our movement keeps showing up because the people of this district are owed answers for years of Keith Self’s and Donald Trump’s failures, from the gas pump to the grocery store to the war nobody voted for. And we keep showing up because every forum reminds us who this seat belongs to. Seniors, parents, veterans, worshippers, neighbors. The folks in these pictures are the whole point of the job. In 16 days, this district can hire a representative who actually represents. Jon Husted is not the only one we’re up against.

With just over two weeks until Election Day, I want to be clear: _Jon Husted’s name is on the ballot, but we can’t forget who’s backing him._ **National Republicans and billionaire donors will do anything to keep Husted in this seat and hold the Senate.**

The GOP has already spent record amounts to boost Husted and defeat us – and crypto PACs are blanketing the airwaves with attack ads distorting my record.

**[So I’m personally asking: Will you chip in $5 now to help us defeat Jon Husted and his super PAC allies and flip this seat?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141694200/654421900/-1024831887?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6562&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZmY1YzZjOC0zYmNiLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_9CCT9uSMgdsz0U9vRsp2NE0AkjBAh8RM2ZGjmd4iRM=)**
Jon Husted and I couldn’t be more different.

**Husted voted to rip health care away from working Ohioans.** I’ve spent my career fighting to expand it.

**Husted is the face of data centers in Ohio.** I think massive corporations should pay for their own electricity.

**Husted voted for the largest tax break for billionaires in American history, the same billionaires bankrolling his campaign.** I stand up for the people who make this country work. Every time.

subject: re: did you get this message?
body:
Peter, I saved your spot

| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter, did you get my email the other day?
I looked over our Victory Captain list this morning, and I didn't see your name yet.
I know how busy life gets, so I wanted to make sure my invitation didn't slip past you.
With less than 20 days to go, there's no time to waste. The people who step up now will decide how this race ends. _**And I want you in that group.**_
Will you take ten seconds right now to accept your Victory Captain role?
[**ACCEPT MY VICTORY CAPTAIN ROLE >>**](https://us.list-manage.com/SKANufsqAYV?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Saying yes means you're ready to stand with me through Election Day, helping your friends and neighbors get to the polls and making sure Central New York hears our message loud and clear.
**I'd be honored to add your name today, Peter.**
Kailee
\-------------------- FORWARDED MESSAGE --------------------To: dpwillis67@gmail.comFrom: Kailee

---
| |
Peter,
We are now 21 days away from Election Day.
When I started this campaign, I said it would be built from the ground up by the people of Central New York. You've been part of that from the start, and I'm grateful.
**But these final weeks are when races like ours are won or lost.**
Every conversation with a neighbor, every reminder to a friend, and every yard sign in a front lawn matters more now than at any point in this campaign.
That is why I'm asking you to become an official VICTORY CAPTAIN for Kailee Buller for Congress.
[**YES, I'LL BE A VICTORY CAPTAIN >>**](https://us.list-manage.com/ZH17iGMujC1?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Here's what being a Victory Captain means...
Victory Captains are the people I'll count on most in the home stretch. You'll be the first to hear our closing plan, the first to get our final campaign updates, and the person your friends and family turn to when they want to know what's really at stake in this race.
_**We'll be counting on you to help make sure the people in your life have a plan to vote, to let us know who could use a yard sign, and to keep us in touch with what's happening in your corner of NY-22.**_
_**You'll be the reason voters who might have stayed home show up instead.**_
I'm running to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our kids can build their futures. And I need people like you standing with me now, more than ever.
[ _So, Peter, will you be there?_](https://us.list-manage.com/K9nyWj1gs22?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| [I'M IN: SIGN ME UP AS A VICTORY CAPTAIN >>](https://us.list-manage.com/dsZ2ZfKrGfL?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| |
The clock is running, and I want my strongest supporters in place before the final push begins.
Thank you for being on this team. Let's finish this together.
Kailee BullerRepublican Candidate for Congress, NY-22

That’s why I’m sharing the money you donate to this campaign with queer advocates and allies across the country in tough races — especially in purple districts where having more people in Congress willing to stand up for LGBTQ+ rights can make a difference. = = = = We need to win next month for the safety of our queer and trans kids. body:
October 18, 2026 | Read Online ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h57v2ppclhoovp46rt8hx68kr/wnh2hghqdkl990h7hx/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvcWR1OGg3aDR4cDIzM3R6d25ubXc3dTg4M2c1d21iNGhrb3Z4OQ== )

From Catherine
--------------

Hi Friend —

Sometimes a few words from someone you love stay with you longer than you expect.

Tuesday was Gregg’s birthday. A member of my family sent him a text that I’ve been thinking about ever since:

Happy Birthday! I ran across a bible verse that made me think of you. It’s Isaiah 6:8.

Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, ‘Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?’ And I said, ‘Here am I. Send me!’

I strive to be that guy. You actually are that guy.

What a thing to say to someone: “I strive to be that guy. You actually are that guy.”

And it’s true about Gregg. In ways seen and unseen, he is always ready to serve. Whatever the assignment, whatever the personal cost, he goes.

But as I reread that message, I began to think about what those words ask of the rest of us.

“Here am I. Send me.”

If you regularly read these letters, you know my familiar closing: “Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW”—for the win. I’ve signed off that way for years, and I still mean every word.

Paul’s call in Ephesians to put on the full armor of God reminds us that readiness to serve is not merely a matter of personality or willpower. We are called to stand firm in faith, truth, righteousness, peace, and prayer, prepared for whatever God places before us.

But lately, I think we’re in an Isaiah 6:8 moment, too. A moment that asks each of us what we are willing to do with the faith we profess and the freedom we’ve been given.

I look around and wonder how so much has changed in our country, in our culture. I worry about what our children are inheriting. Some days, it’s hard to know what to believe or where to begin.

Then I remember: our time here is not an accident. We have work to do.

These midterm elections will help determine how much harder that work becomes. The choice matters. If we preserve liberty, we preserve the ability to correct our mistakes, challenge our leaders, and keep working toward something better. Every freedom we surrender makes that work harder.

Honest elections. Safe communities. An immigration system that works. The opportunity to build a life through our own efforts. A government that respects its constitutional limits. These are reasonable expectations of a free country, and we should have the confidence to insist on them.

America has come through bitter divisions and dangerous days before. Each generation has had to decide what it would preserve, what it would repair, and what it would pass on. Now that responsibility belongs to us.

By 2028, I believe advances in artificial intelligence will have changed daily life in ways we are only beginning to understand. As technology grows more powerful, we will need to be even more deliberate about protecting human freedom, human judgment, and our connections to one another.

Which brings me back to that birthday text—and to 7 Votes ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h57v2ppclhoovp46rt8hx68kr/vqh3hrho6vq2x2hghl/aHR0cHM6Ly83dm90ZXMub3Jn ).

We do not have to know everything the future holds to accept responsibility for what we can do today.

Start with seven people you know. Reach out. Help them make a plan to vote. Their 7 Votes ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/k0uzok29gmh6h57v2ppclhoovp46rt8hx68kr/vqh3hrho6vq2x2hghl/aHR0cHM6Ly83dm90ZXMub3Jn ) profile gives them a place to check their registration, find where to vote, and get local voting information. Stay in touch through Election Day.

There is something powerful in that simple act of connection. A friend hears from a friend. Someone who feels forgotten knows they matter. Someone who might have stayed home has a plan—and someone encouraging them to follow through.

We strengthen our country through those relationships. We keep our humanity by caring for one another. And we defend freedom by exercising it and helping others do the same.

For these next two weeks, let’s invite everyone we can to vote. Let’s speak plainly about what freedom makes possible. Let’s give people a reason to believe their participation matters, and help them act on it.

There is still so much good in this country. So much worth protecting. So much we can do.

The question before us is familiar: “Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?”

Let’s answer it together.

Here am I. Send me.

Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 AND Isaiah 6:8 FTW! God will never leave nor forsake us — let’s gooooo!

Ever onward —

clean_body: October 18, 2026 | Read Online ( == ) From Catherine Hi Friend — Sometimes a few words from someone you love stay with you longer than you expect. Tuesday was Gregg’s birthday. A member of my family sent him a text that I’ve been thinking about ever since: Happy Birthday! I ran across a bible verse that made me think of you. It’s Isaiah 6:8. Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, ‘Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?’ And I said, ‘Here am I. Send me!’ I strive to be that guy. You actually are that guy. What a thing to say to someone: “I strive to be that guy. You actually are that guy.” And it’s true about Gregg. In ways seen and unseen, he is always ready to serve. Whatever the assignment, whatever the personal cost, he goes. But as I reread that message, I began to think about what those words ask of the rest of us. “Here am I. Send me.” If you regularly read these letters, you know my familiar closing: “Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW”—for the win. I’ve signed off that way for years, and I still mean every word. Paul’s call in Ephesians to put on the full armor of God reminds us that readiness to serve is not merely a matter of personality or willpower. We are called to stand firm in faith, truth, righteousness, peace, and prayer, prepared for whatever God places before us. But lately, I think we’re in an Isaiah 6:8 moment, too. A moment that asks each of us what we are willing to do with the faith we profess and the freedom we’ve been given. I look around and wonder how so much has changed in our country, in our culture. I worry about what our children are inheriting. Some days, it’s hard to know what to believe or where to begin. Then I remember: our time here is not an accident. We have work to do. These midterm elections will help determine how much harder that work becomes. The choice matters. If we preserve liberty, we preserve the ability to correct our mistakes, challenge our leaders, and keep working toward something better. Every freedom we surrender makes that work harder. Honest elections. Safe communities. An immigration system that works. The opportunity to build a life through our own efforts. A government that respects its constitutional limits. These are reasonable expectations of a free country, and we should have the confidence to insist on them. America has come through bitter divisions and dangerous days before. Each generation has had to decide what it would preserve, what it would repair, and what it would pass on. Now that responsibility belongs to us. By 2028, I believe advances in artificial intelligence will have changed daily life in ways we are only beginning to understand. As technology grows more powerful, we will need to be even more deliberate about protecting human freedom, human judgment, and our connections to one another. Which brings me back to that birthday text—and to 7 Votes ( ). We do not have to know everything the future holds to accept responsibility for what we can do today. Start with seven people you know. Reach out. Help them make a plan to vote. Their 7 Votes ( ) profile gives them a place to check their registration, find where to vote, and get local voting information. Stay in touch through Election Day. There is something powerful in that simple act of connection. A friend hears from a friend. Someone who feels forgotten knows they matter. Someone who might have stayed home has a plan—and someone encouraging them to follow through. We strengthen our country through those relationships. We keep our humanity by caring for one another. And we defend freedom by exercising it and helping others do the same. For these next two weeks, let’s invite everyone we can to vote. Let’s speak plainly about what freedom makes possible. Let’s give people a reason to believe their participation matters, and help them act on it. There is still so much good in this country. So much worth protecting. So much we can do. The question before us is familiar: “Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?” Let’s answer it together. Here am I. Send me. Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 AND Isaiah 6:8 FTW! God will never leave nor forsake us — let’s gooooo! Ever onward — P.S. — If you can support our work, please do. We are pushing hard! Those numbers will grow exponentially by Election Day — and it will make a difference! This year’s races will be close!! Every vote counts! Please support the work if you can. | | | | | Saudi Arabia figured it out.

They pay their citizens $3,600 a month per family. Just for existing. Funded entirely by oil.

Meanwhile, politicians in America are arguing about Twitter, while you get nothing from the $300 billion we generate from oil and gas every year.

[But there is a way to collect.](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=ea1d528efc15490190194d7e1f9c5ed6&_e=ht_ofeNouxGPJGW20IWP0z5Z2ywYlJaLHhHVzQqSlLz-6z6NFJl3nZZMsg4jtAzkCLA0uIEgvGNbW2aN22U-RMNUDk2fNMAWu-7Ux9-HnATAvV51SLi1b9qr0eK4V3xym_PkUzItTFi51rdzbydFDLT8YqkhxX_EVvb5zXUdZxQs3LdtXVK40h7qm1R6e0KTIz57RtSAgvQqX-sQ2IlZQ7K75Jc-o4cuQU-HPYrEtBVIZUxvn6HoABDhpsxAZ_cADZ-l8VPCtrjnfHY35rihM2UjOqc_12QvC-abC8uJjE7wt6q47GIfBLRIJsSft9RIliov81UkZA4medqvq90--tM3xO50LnMCY5cd8XtEQeuinIK6X1FEWb7ReDyKAsov3Me06cPRlmq6KqujDEpJXA1OH3GmQShXWHaOQUiOZnCLG3FV2PFmRkldsAVOYremdEsUhMXuBOham2s2-U7DwbLQnmRnTePH2SLgax2Yx7KNCzXqEckmgUR6pZEOYCci8exfPQOirosoMcZrNMBhut-EnaQ-un3Fht62MX-j79E%3D)

It's called the Patriot Income Plan, or P.I.P. for short.

It's not a government program. It's not a stimulus check. It's not tied to an election or a budget vote.

It's direct ownership in 14 entities that control America's energy infrastructure — pipelines, terminals, processing plants — and pay 10% a year to everyone who holds units.

Put in $10,000 = get $1,000 back.
Put in $50,000 = get $5,000 back.
Put in $100,000 = get $10,000 back.

42 payouts a year. Deposited automatically.

This is universal basic income for people who don't want to wait around for the government to figure it out.

P.I.P. is on pace to pay out $53 billion this year — a record. The next distribution drops in days.

[Here's how to enroll](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=ea1d528efc15490190194d7e1f9c5ed6&_e=ht_ofeNouxGPJGW20IWP0z5Z2ywYlJaLHhHVzQqSlLz-6z6NFJl3nZZMsg4jtAzkCLA0uIEgvGNbW2aN22U-RMNUDk2fNMAWu-7Ux9-HnATAvV51SLi1b9qr0eK4V3xym_PkUzItTFi51rdzbydFDLT8YqkhxX_EVvb5zXUdZxR8mM1Np38wGpm0Tsdz9TsRk7KX_OFoCGspnzrvmWm7AUhRfmPx-giK_ogrur3VK476tb4vgGTGPruD2PLVIEouowNJ0qpBwX6FX-ey9PfA6ADJvKU7ZMRBynXnfn1mbkx595g0wGfuu7cq22HOANn7CDH6x_W5YB9cA4v3o1McA3n1DCjmkht87gn8mCnTJswjR5sZuoJ-JaAYiyjAjxevIcY5oEJN3b59LAmNlzyOvh7Fo2zFjfsvwWBTMGJplCvoMpnQKCPmNFUHwrMW7kf4uOas3Lucpy5M-aZztniTW66Tn_bONNNimnf72xDabSBnimsALQL-kGdHbIj2NHAiMVmDpyieM_QvU6SMfL4BuH35v1wAl5nKl5OPQT5UAQw%3D)

| | | |
---
Case File No DRT-ED-TOLL · Special File · America’s Toll Roads
America Is Producing More Natural Gas Than Ever. The Companies That Move It Get Paid on Every Molecule.
U.S. gas production hit a record in 2025 and is expected to rise again this year and next. Exports are at records too. Nearly all of it flows through pipelines, terminals and processing plants owned by companies that collect fees and pass much of that cash on to their owners.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Most people think energy money comes from drilling. But drilling is a gamble on prices. The steadier business is moving the oil and gas once it comes out of the ground. Like a toll road, it gets paid on volume, whether prices are high or low.
The evidence board
| | The Numbers Behind the Boom
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — record production.** According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, America produced a record 107.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas a day in 2025. It expects 111.7 billion this year and 115.9 billion in 2027.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — record exports.** LNG exports hit a record 15.1 billion cubic feet a day in 2025, and the EIA expects 17.4 billion in 2026.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — record volumes.** One of the largest pipeline partnerships moved a record 14.7 million barrels a day in the second quarter, and its cash flow covered its payouts almost twice over.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the payouts.** As of July 31, a major index of energy infrastructure partnerships yielded about 6.5%, and companies making up 88% of the largest MLP fund had raised payouts from a year earlier.
| OUR THEORY
---
As long as America keeps pumping and exporting more energy, the owners of the pipes get paid more. That’s a simple business model, and it’s why so much of the cash it produces ends up in the pockets of the people who own a piece of it.
Connected file
| | Why Steady Income Matters Right Now
---|---
Stocks have been setting record after record this year, and the midterm elections are just weeks away, on November 3. According to LPL Research, midterm years have historically seen the biggest average market pullback of the four-year presidential cycle, about 17.5%. The good news: the S&P; 500 has risen in the 12 months after every midterm since 1954.
That’s why some veteran investors are urging people to get their money positioned before Election Day.

Peter, The U.S. Supreme Court has done serious damage to our democracy this year, especially by gutting the Voting Rights Act — the crowning achievement of the Civil Rights Movement. But SCOTUS isn’t the only court that’s hurt the cause of free and fair elections. A.G. Holder is calling our attention to the high courts that don’t get enough attention for their role in setting the course for our democracy: “There are state supreme courts that protected voting rights and struck down gerrymanders. And there are state supreme courts that allowed really reckless politicians to make it harder for American citizens to vote. So state supreme courts are extremely important guardians of democracy and people’s liberty.” And yet most of us aren’t hearing much about the critical state supreme court elections happening in just a few weeks. The NDRC is focused on electing Democracy Defenders running for the bench in three key states: Jennifer Brunner in Ohio, Anita Earls in North Carolina, and Megan Cavanagh and Noah Hood in Michigan. These judges have records of defending democracy — and we need them in office to push back on extreme gerrymanders and ensure equal justice under the law. Holder in the fight to elect fair-minded state supreme court justices | Peter, The U.S. Supreme Court has done serious damage to our democracy this year, especially by gutting the Voting Rights Act — the crowning achievement of the Civil Rights Movement. But SCOTUS isn’t the only court that’s hurt the cause of free and fair elections. A.G. Holder is calling our attention to the high courts that don’t get enough attention for their role in setting the course for our democracy: “There are state supreme courts that protected voting rights and struck down gerrymanders. So state supreme courts are extremely important guardians of democracy and people’s liberty.” And yet most of us aren’t hearing much about the critical state supreme court elections happening in just a few weeks. The NDRC is focused on electing Democracy Defenders running for the bench in three key states: Jennifer Brunner in Ohio, Anita Earls in North Carolina, and Megan Cavanagh and Noah Hood in Michigan. Martin isn’t on the ballot this November, but the work that brought us together doesn’t pause between elections. Every day, New Mexicans are working hard for their families, caring for their communities, and looking toward a future where opportunity is within reach. They deserve leaders who will keep fighting for working families, protect our public lands, advance clean energy, and stand up for our democracy. That is the work Martin is continuing in the U.S. Senate — and it matters whether there is an election around the corner or not. Campaigns are about more than one Election Day. They are about building a community that believes New Mexico’s people and future are worth fighting for. They are about staying connected to the values we share: bringing down costs, protecting the places we love, ensuring our government answers to working families in New Mexico, and challenging the corruption and MAGA extremism of the Trump administration that has harmed so many families. That's why we continue to ask for your support between elections. Your contributions allow us to keep this community engaged, share Martin's work in the Senate, support candidates throughout New Mexico and across the country, and build the grassroots strength we'll need in the fights ahead. We'll continue keeping you updated on Martin's work in the Senate, asking for your input on the issues that matter to you, and reaching out for your support — including contributions when you're able to give. Every way you engage helps more than you might know, whether Martin is on the ballot or not. Because government should answer to you. Yes, he outraised us again, and he has more than four times as much cash as we do. But look at what he's done with all that money. Abbott has spent $141.3 million so far this year, including $74 million in the last three months alone. That's six times what we spent over the same stretch. Think about that for a second. Abbott's team called a recent poll showing Gina ahead "garbage." **But you don't spend $141 million in nine months unless you're worried about losing.** And he has reason to be. Four public polls in the last three weeks have shown Gina narrowly ahead. Before last month, Abbott had never trailed in a single public poll in any of his four campaigns for governor. **Texans are fed up with his record on property taxes and data centers, and it's showing.** The funding behind these campaigns tells a lot of the story. Abbott's biggest checks over the last few months? $1 million apiece from billionaires like Jeff Yass and Kenneth Fisher. Ours came overwhelmingly from regular people: more than 136,000 donors giving an average of $53. Nearly three out of four of them had never given to Gina before. We don't need billionaire checks to win this election. We just need to keep doing what's working: raising the resources we need to compete and communicating our message with the Texans who need to hear it. FirstName, early voting starts October 19. **We have less than a week to make sure voters hear Gina's message before they head to the polls, and Abbott is going to spend every dollar he has left trying to drown it out.
